text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 index set another record close, its ninth of the past 11 sessions, as the market extended its record-breaking post-election surge, boosted from the outset by an overnight Dow record -- and with selected shares squeezed sharply higher by a shortage of stock in the market -- the blue chip UK index ended 12.7 points higher at 4,693.9, up 63 from last week.

FRANKFURT - German shares closed bourse trade at a record high lifted by Wall Street's strong gains, and the firmer dollar which was boosted by markets' perceptions Europe's common currency Euro might now be weaker, in light of Germany's scramble to fill budgetary holes, seen as fudging EMU goals. The 30-share DAX index closed up 42.44 points at 3,604.55, a gain of 42.14 on the week. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,569.26.

PARIS - French stocks rose to a third consecutive record close after a ground-breaking advance on Wall Street helped lift the bourse's leading index over the 2,800 mark. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 8.27 points or 0.3 percent to 2,784.28, rising 150.37 from last Friday. ZURICH - Swiss shares ended a strong week with their fifth consecutive record despite giving up most of their early gains towards the end of the session on profit taking and an easier Wall Street opening, stocks such CS Group, Roche and Novartis were also influenced by derivatives-linked transactions. The All-share Swiss Performance Index was up 9.94 points or 0.31 percent to 3,255.86, up 88.04 from seven days ago.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended moderately higher, as issues driven by domestic demand, such as Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, attracted investors due to the yen's recent firmness against the dollar, the market was somewhat cautious ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting next week, which may affect Wall Street stocks. The 225-share Nikkei average gained 268.42 points or 1.34 percent to finish at 20,324.73, rising 521.95 on the week.

HONG KONG - After spending much of the day in negative territory, Hong Kong stocks closed modestly higher as leading blue chips reversed early losses. The Hang Seng Index gained 20.47 points or 0.15 percent to close at 14,062.37. up 131.57 from last Friday.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market was locked in a record high closing level with renewed buying interest in the key resources stocks overcoming a battered banking sector. The All Ordinaries index added 13.1 to 2,538.1, a rise of 12.1 from seven days ago.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended stunted in directionless trade with industrials gasping at lower levels and gold finishing weaker despite bullion's recent recoveries, sentiment in the industrials sector had continued to worsen after poor results from some of the market's key industrial companies. The Industrial index finished down 19.4 points at 8,421.2, down 80.0 on the week, the Gold index was down 26.8 points at 1,228.3, a drop of 9.3 from last Friday and the All-share down 30.3 points at 7,142.8, falling 36.6 from last week.
